patient_information: A 12-year-old boy from rural north-west Kenya.
chief_complaint: Painful, watery, red eyes, worse in the sun, and struggling to keep eyes open for 2 months.
history_of_present_illness: Six months previously, he was treated at a dispensary with tetracycline eye ointment for less severe symptoms, which did not improve. He then went to a traditional healer who applied juice extracts from the ecucuka plant (Aloe vera species), after which he experienced severe eye pain, discharge, very red eyes, and could hardly see.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The boy lives with his parents in Loima, Turkana County, a hot, dusty and dry area of Kenya, fetching water from a dried riverbed about 6 kilometres from home, keeping herds of cows and sheep, and helping with herding and watering.
physical_exam: Very poor vision in both eyes: visual acuity is 6/60 with the left eye, and he can only perceive hand movements with the right eye. Examination showed lid scarring, trichiasis, extensive corneal opacification, and severely inflamed conjunctiva.
differential_diagnosis: Corneal and conjunctival damage from use of traditional eye medicine, trachomatous trichiasis, and vitamin A deficiency.
management_and_clinical_course: He was admitted and given oral azithromycin and oral vitamin A supplements. He was referred to an ophthalmologist for lid surgery to redress trichiasis and for a conjunctival flap to seal the corneal defect.
final_diagnosis: Bilateral trachomatous trichiasis (TT), corneal opacity (CO), and a left perforating corneal ulcer, possibly exacerbated by traditional medicine.

tables.title: Findings on Inspection of Both Eyes
rows: Fibrotic lids with loss of lid architecture and tightening of palpebral aperture Loss of lashes from lower lid, misdirected and in-turned upper lid lashes (trichiasis)
Lids swollen, mucus deposits, eyelashes misdirected Eversion of lower lid margin
Severely inflamed > 5 follicles (subepithelial inflammatory foci) identified on eversion of lids Scarring of the upper tarsal conjunctivae
Diffuse corneal opacification (scarring) with central thinning and irregular surface Fibrovascular pannus on the upper cornea
Focal inferocentral corneal scars, one with adherent iris indicating previous perforation Thin central cornea
